cards.title: 零件里面，怎么还有零件
cards.scene: CARD 1. A medium-wide interior view of a cluttered but cozy SMALL WORKSHOP. BAKA-01 sits at the workbench exhausted but endearing, one original pincer holding a little hammer and the other turning an unfolded recipe sheet. Neat and chaotic piles of gear wheels, small iron plates, rubber rings and tools surround the robot. A large corkboard and bench are covered with hand-drawn pictogram sticky-note dependency arrows: one part requires several other parts, finally an arrow curls back toward BAKA's head. The two cyan LED eyes convey dizzy overwhelmed tiredness, with restrained manga swirl marks above the head. Do not put literal gear eyes or alter the face anatomy. Warm overhead work lamp, cyan CRT and a modest pink tube light. Indoor walls and shelves fill background. No wearable exoskeleton yet: this is BEFORE its invention. A funny tactile handmade assembly predicament, warm and sympathetic. All little notes use component drawings, no readable prose.

cards.title: 给双手补上一点工作经验
cards.scene: CARD 2. SAME workshop, a warmer hopeful quiet night scene, three-quarter medium view. BAKA-01 has invented and wears a compact mechanical exoskeleton OVER its RIGHT original metal pincer/wrist: scuffed brass wrist cuff, tiny exposed gears, restrained pink/cyan wires and two slim auxiliary mechanical tool fingers that assist the existing pincer. Clearly an ATTACHMENT to the same robot arm, not a replacement human hand, not a separate sentient robot, no giant new arms. This precise wearable should stay consistent in later cards. BAKA rests the box head on its LEFT forearm on a soft folded shop cloth, cyan eyes are two sleepy closed arcs. The RIGHT attached mechanical hand continues assembling a little gear component safely away from its resting head. A small battered CRT beside the work has a clear icon-only vertical queue: raw materials → intermediate gear → finished component, connected by arrows with checkmarks, conveying sequential automated crafting while the owner dozes. Completed gears and rubber rings neatly arranged in a small tray. Warm yellow lamp and gentle lilac shadows. No large factory or garbage mountain.

cards.title: 毕业作品，被归进了原料区
cards.scene: CARD 3. Interior warehouse with orderly labeled bins and shelves. BAKA-01 proudly wears a clearly homemade flat GRADUATION CAP made from brown cardboard (antenna still visible), holding a small box of carefully crafted gear wheels, iron plates and rubber seals. Its cyan eyes have just shifted from pride to funny stunned realization. The compact brass wrist/pincer exoskeleton invented in card 2 remains worn on its right wrist. A huge unfolding illustrated industrial equipment catalog sprawls across the table: the cherished tiny parts are diagrammatically pointed into small construction positions inside a much larger gearbox/steam machine. Foreground a little shelf label with only the word '原料' is pasted over an older tag, visually reclassifying the precious finished products as basic ingredients. Keep text minimal: '原料' and the BAKA-01 badge only. Warm lived-in indoor warehouse, violet shelving shadows, cyan diagram glow. No actual large machines freely built: the big equipment is ONLY drawn in the open catalog. The graduation cap and box provide the comic contrast.

cards.title: 大机器没有小胃口
cards.scene: CARD 4. A whimsical IMAGINED visual metaphor emerging from an open industrial catalog INSIDE the warehouse/workshop. Three oversized personified industrial MACHINE diners loom around a long cafeteria table: a brass gearbox/transmission machine, a squat round steam boiler and an assembly press. They are recognizably EQUIPMENT with funny hungry hatch-mouths and simple expressive gauges, not independent humanoid robots. They hold small placards showing pictograms only of gears/metal plates, fuel chunks and water drops; empty big trays wait in front of them. In the low foreground, tiny BAKA-01 in exact original outfit and identity timidly offers its small precious box of components, with the compact brass right-wrist attachment setting down one comically tiny fork. Robot cyan eyes are deadpan alarmed. The imagined equipment/table has slightly dreamy lilac manga cloud/ink edges rising from the catalog, while the real indoor shelves/bench frame the composition. Funny appetite/scale contrast, zero menace, zero actual eating of BAKA, no humans, no dialogue, no captions.

cards.title: 工厂开饭了
cards.scene: CARD 5. Wide cinematic INSIDE view looking from the cozy packed little workshop doorway into a large EMPTY industrial hall with tall windows and steel beams. BAKA-01 has taken off its cardboard graduation cap (it sits on a nearby crate), now wears simple transparent shop safety goggles perched on top of the unchanged cream head without obscuring cyan eyes/antenna. Still has teal scarf, mustard torso, pincer hands, red boots and the SAME compact brass right-wrist attachment. It is excited and determined, running colored string/tape lines across the empty floor to lay out the FIRST real production line; the auxiliary tool fingers hold the plan while the other pincer measures. Faint translucent pale-purple hand-drawn PLANNING outlines of future conveyor routes, gear-drive machines and a small steaming boiler appear only as imagined overlay on otherwise empty floor, clearly not already built or materialized machinery. Warm peach light through high windows, neon cyan/pink workshop spill, a hopeful ambitious reveal of scale. Focus on one consistent BAKA and room-scale planning, NOT an outdoor dump or already completed giant industrial city. No readable text except chest badge.
